idiom_name: kotlinx.html builder DSL / string templates + buildString
implementation_notes: Kotlin's idiom is the kotlinx.html builder DSL - appendHTML(), div { }, ul { li { +album.title } } - where receiver-scoped builders replace the Transformer class and the unary plus appends escaped text; buildString with string templates covers small fragments without a library. On the JVM the javax.xml.transform and javax.xml.stream APIs remain available for XML output. A transformer object is still justified when markup is one of several formats behind a shared interface.
pitfalls: String templates interpolate raw values: escaping is not automatic, so buildString fragments need an explicit escape helper (kotlinx.html escapes +content for you).
kotlinx.html's streaming builders write to a Writer/Appendable immediately: a failure mid-build leaves a half-written response unless the response can be reset.
Nested builders change the receiver scope: capture outer values in locals before entering a builder block or name resolution produces surprising output.
